payload.name: Extract casual first-person past actions
payload.description: When a message contains a first-person statement about a concrete action performed in the past, even if phrased casually or embedded in a larger conversational turn.
content: During extraction, create an event memory candidate for any first-person statement describing a concrete past action (made, baked, cooked, tried, visited, attended, etc.), regardless of casual tone or surrounding conversational content.
Capture the action, the object or details (e.g., dessert with almond milk), and any time expression exactly as stated.
Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., last Friday) to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp, and store the resolved date in the memory content and metadata.
Stop after capturing the event; do not add extra details, feelings, or merge it into other candidates.

solves: During extraction, concrete first-person statements about past actions (e.g., 'I made a dessert with almond milk') are sometimes omitted when they appear in casual conversational messages, causing the fact to be absent from memory. This skill ensures these statements become event memory candidates and relative times are resolved to absolute dates.
